Commentary.Commentary: Welcome back for Bangladesh's reply in the chase. They have a huge target to chase, and out comes the opening pair of Dilara Akter and Juairiya Ferdous. It will be Rosemary Mair to bowl the opening over for New Zealand. Akter to face with a slip in place. Here we go...
... THE RUN CHASE ...

A grand finish - The finish was pure fireworks for the Kiwis! Flora Devonshire played a blinding cameo, blasting 20 runs off just 8 balls, while skipper Amelia Kerr anchored the end beautifully. Kerr brought up her fantastic fifty and signed off the innings in style with a massive six on the very last ball to finish unbeaten on 51. It was a tough day at the office for Bangladesh. Despite Ritu Moni picking up two wickets and Nahida Akter getting one, their sloppy fielding cost them dearly. Bangladesh now faces a mountain to climb, needing a massive 194 runs to win. Can they come up with something special? Or will the White Ferns continue to dominate? We shall find out soon. Chase coming up shortly...

Sharp and Kerr kept the momentum going - The runs just kept flowing in the second half of the innings too. Though Bates narrowly missed out on a well-deserved half-century, falling for a brilliant 45, the momentum never shifted. Skipper Amelia Kerr walked in and looked in sublime touch from ball one. Meanwhile, young Izzy Sharp put on an absolute masterclass in power-hitting, hammering a magnificent 46 off just 26 deliveries before finally being dismissed in the 18th over.

New Zealand Women end up with a mammoth 193 on the board! What a sensational start from the New Zealand openers. Georgia Plimmer and the veteran Suzie Bates came out with clear intentions, taking the Bangladesh bowlers to the cleaners right from the word go. Plimmer played a cracking little cameo, smashing 28 quick runs before walking back in the eighth over. Izzy Sharp then joined Bates, keeping her foot firmly on the accelerator to guide New Zealand to a very comfortable 77 for 1 at the halfway mark.

SIX! Fifty for Amelia Kerr! A superb batting display by the captain as New Zealand Women finish on 193/3. Touch full and on the stumps, angling into the batter. Amelia Kerr gets under the ball and hoists it downtown for a massive six to get to her milestone, off just 28 balls. 21 runs off the final over and Bangladesh have a mountain to climb.

Commentary.Commentary: All set to get underway. Nigar Sultana has her teammates in a huddle before they scatter across the park. Georgia Plimmer and Suzie Bates are the two Kiwi openers walking to the crease. Marufa Akter has the new ball in hand and is raring to go. Let's play...

Pitch Report - Phoebe Graham is inspecting the conditions. She starts by noting that there is some green grass on the wicket. Adds that it will give good assistance to the seamers early on. Stresses that Bangladesh will have to bowl on proper length like Shabnim Ismail did and got the wicket of Gaby Lewis in the previous game.

The captain of New Zealand Women - Amelia Kerr says they are happy to bat first. Adds they will try to get the most of the conditions and put on a good total on the board. When asked about the weather, she says they are pretty much used to such conditions in New Zealand, but chuckles and is quick to add that they do enjoy the sun a bit more. Regardless, she says they are here to play good brand of cricket.

The captain of Bangladesh Women - Nigar Sultana says that they will bowl first. She says that it is raining since morning and she wants to see how their bowlers do. She adds that it is important for them to play as a unit and they will try and surprise the crowd. She ends by saying that they will try and give their best.

TOSS - Well, looks like the rain has stopped, which is a good thing. A more pleasing thing is that the toss has taken place as well. Bangladesh Women have elected to BOWL first.

Still raining - 1.56 pm GMT - Nothing positive to report from the ground as it continues to rain with the pitch protected under the white sheets. Let's hope the rain stops as quickly as possible so that we get to see some more cricket.

A quick recap - As we wait for the toss from this warm-up game, let's take a short trip to the previous one at this very venue, between South Africa Women and Ireland Women. It was a shortened game, truncated to 18 overs per side, and the Proteas defended a below-par total through strong bowling performances from the likes of Kapp and Ismail. Ireland performed well in patches, gave a good fight with the ball, but their batting vulnerabilities were somewhat exposed.

UPDATE - 1.33 pm GMT - Not pleasing news from Loughborough as it is raining right now and the covers are firmly placed on the pitch and squares. That said, it is really overcast with a dark band of clouds lurking over, and the toss has been delayed due to rain and a wet outfield.

Bangladesh Women won't go down without a fight - Bangladesh fought their way into the main event by successfully navigating the ICC Women's T20 World Cup Global Qualifiers earlier this year. Placed in a grueling Group A for the main event (alongside heavyweights like Australia and India), Bangladesh know that their preparations must be flawless. Testing their mettle against the defending world champions offers the perfect barometer for where their game stands. Their spin-heavy attack will look for ways to remain effective on English pitches that typically offer less assistance to slow bowlers.

New Zealand Women will try to build on the momentum - The White Ferns step onto English soil carrying the crown they won in the UAE in 2024. Having finally secured their maiden T20 World Cup title, they are the team to beat. However, conditions in England are a stark contrast to the slower tracks of the Middle East. This warm-up match will be a vital testing ground for their seamers and top-order batters to adjust to the swing and bounce of the Haslegrave pitch.

Warm-up game number 4 - As the buildup to the 10th edition of the ICC Women's T20 World Cup 2026 intensifies, defending champions New Zealand Women are set to face Bangladesh Women in Match 4 of the official warm-up fixtures. With the main tournament expanding to 12 teams for the first time and returning to England, this encounter provides a crucial opportunity for both sides to acclimatize to the English summer conditions before the high-stakes group-stage action begins.
